newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW-UK Q3 GDP, Aug/Sept trade data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-UK Q3 GDP, Aug/Sept trade data.

text.p: Following is a list of reactions to UK Q3 GDP, Sept non-EU trade and August global trade data.

GDP rose 0.8 pct q-q (vs expected +0.7 pct) and 2.3 pct y-y (vs expected +2.3 pct). The global trade def was 584 million stg in Aug and Sept's non-EU def was 851 million stg (vs expected 730 million).

"This is very much the higher end of forecasts. Unless they'e done any major backward revisions this will be the fastest quarter on quarter growth since the end of 1994. It may cause people to start revising up their GDP forcasts...for next year."

"These are strong figures and confirm the economy is gathering momentum...but there is a mixed picture across sectors. On the back of these figures the Bank of England will be itching to urge a rate hike. They could do it next week but I feel it would make more sense to wait until after the budget. If we have a cautious budget and I think we will have a cautious budget, and if sterling continues to strengthen and inflation data is good, you could still get a justifiable rate cut by the end of the year."
MARION BELL, ROYAL BANK OF SCOTLAND

"The first estimate of UK Q3 GDP confirmed forcasts of above trend growth. A continued strong service sector...compensated for still sluggish manufacturing. For 1997 we forecast 3.5 percent growth, with the risk on the upside. We doubt there is enough spare capacity to allow near term falls in inflation that other analysts forecast. These data are gilt and short stg negative and stg positive."

The GDP data was pretty much in line though the services output was a little stronger than expected. In terms of policy, there's something here for both Clarke and George. Clarke can point to annual GDP growth of 2.3 percent which is still below trend and George can say if you annualize the quarter-on-quarter rate you get growth above 3.0 percent which is certainly above the Bank's estimate of trend.
